title: Baek Jong-won–Style White Kimchi (Baek-kimchi)
summary: A small-batch, non-spicy napa cabbage kimchi adapted from SBS's Delicious Rendezvous. Clear Korean lemon-lime soda and salted shrimp give the brine a refreshing savory flavor.

steps.description: Cut the half head of napa cabbage lengthwise into two wedges. Dissolve 105g coarse salt in 1.5L water, submerge the cabbage, and brine for 2–3 hours, turning once. The thick white ribs should bend without snapping.
Rinse the salted cabbage 2–3 times under running water, then set it upside down in a colander to drain for about 30 minutes.
Whisk 6g sweet rice flour into 200ml taken from the 1L of kimchi-brine water. Cook over low heat, stirring for 2–3 minutes, to make a thin slurry. Let it cool completely.
Julienne the 1/4 radish, cut the scallions into 5cm lengths, and slice the red chili pepper thinly on the diagonal.

Blend the onion, 40g saeujeot, 40g minced garlic, and 125ml lemon-lime soda. Mix with the cooled rice slurry and the remaining 800ml brine water. Strain through a fine sieve if you prefer a clearer brine.
Gently mix the radish, scallions, and red chili. Tuck small portions between the leaves of the well-drained cabbage.

Pack the stuffed cabbage snugly into a clean, narrow, deep, lidded container. Pour in the brine from step 5 and use a clean fermentation weight or small plate to keep the cabbage beneath the liquid. The roughly 1.2L of prepared brine may not cover the cabbage in a wider container; if necessary, prepare and add more of the step-5 brine using the same ingredient proportions.
Leave covered in a cool spot out of direct sunlight for 12–24 hours, then refrigerate. Let mature for another 1–2 days in the fridge; taste and cut into serving pieces.
